name: GO Classes Test Series 2025 | NIELIT Mock Test 7

question.text:
Mr. Vivek walks $6$ meters North-east, then turns and walks $6$ meters South-east, both at 60 degrees to east. He further moves $2$ meters South and $4$ meters West. What is the straight distance in meters between the point he started from and the point he finally reached?

  1. $2\sqrt 2$
  2. $2$
  3. $\sqrt 2$
  4. $1/\sqrt2$

​​​​$\text{P, Q, R, S}$, and $\text{T}$ have launched a new startup. Two of them are siblings. The office of the startup has just three rooms. All of them agree that the siblings should not share the same room.

If $\text{S}$ and $\text{Q}$ are single children, and the room allocations shown below are acceptable to all.
$$\begin{array}{|l|l|l|}
\hline \text{PR} & \text{TS} & \text{Q} \\
\hline
\end{array}$$$$\begin{array}{|l|l|l|}
\hline \text{PQ} & \text{RT} & \text{S} \\
\hline
\end{array}$$

then, which one of the given options is the siblings?

  1. $\mathrm{P}$ and $\mathrm{T}$
  2. $\mathrm{P}$ and $\mathrm{S}$
  3. $\mathrm{T}$ and $\mathrm{Q}$
  4. $\mathrm{T}$ and $\mathrm{R}$

In four-digit integer numbers from $1001$ to $9999$, the digit group $\text{“37”}$ (in the same sequence) appears ________ times.

  1. $270$
  2. $279$
  3. $280$
  4. $299$

1. Some football players play cricket.
  2. All cricket players play hockey.

Among the options given below, the statement that logically follows from the two statements $1$ and $2$ above, is :

  1. No football player plays hockey
  2. Some football players play hockey
  3. All football players play hockey
  4. All hockey players play football

Lauren plays basketball with her friends. She makes 10 baskets. Each of these baskets is worth either 2 or 3 points. Lauren scores a total of 26 points. How many 3 point baskets did she make?

  1. 5
  2. 6
  3. 7
  4. 8

The digits $A$ and $B$ make the multiplication below correct. What is $A+B$?

  1. 4
  2. 6

A spinner is divided into 3 equal sections, as shown.

An arrow is attached to the centre of the spinner. The arrow is spun twice. What is the probability that the arrow lands on the same colour twice?

Kathy owns more cats than Alice and more dogs than Bruce. Alice owns more dogs than Kathy and fewer cats than Bruce. Which of the statements must be true?

  1. Bruce owns the fewest cats
  2. Bruce owns the most cats.
  3. Kathy owns the most cats.
  4. Alice owns the most dogs.

Choose the word from the questions given below that is most nearly opposite in meaning to the given word:
$\textbf{Frequency}$

  1. periodicity
  2. rarity
  3. gradualness
  4. persistency

A flower never changes more than once per night.
This is what the magic garden looks like one morning:

What will the magic garden look like after four nights have passed?

Seven identical square pieces of paper were labelled with the letters $A$ through G. These papers were then placed on a table one at a time, in some order, ending with the paper labelled E. The diagram shows the view from above. In what order were the papers placed on the table?

Please note that E is placed on top and is completely visible, and all the other papers are of the same size and identical squares.

  1. $C, A, D, B, G, F, E$
  2. $C, A, B, D, F, G, E$
  3. $F, G, C, A, D, B, E$

The remainder when 111 is divided by 10 is 1. The remainder when 111 is divided by the positive integer $n$ is 6. The number of possible values of $n$ is ______.

  1. 5
  2. 8
  3. 7
  4. 6

One of the parts $(A, B, C, D)$ in the sentence given below contains an ERROR. Which one of the following is INCORRECT?

I requested that he should be given the driving test today instead of tomorrow.

  1. requested that
  2. should be given
  3. the driving test
  4. instead of tomorrow

If the sum of the first $20$ consecutive positive odd numbers is divided by $20^{2}$, the result is

  1. $1$
  2. $20$
  3. $2$
  4. $1 / 2$

If $f\left ( x \right ) = 2 \:\ln \left ( \sqrt{e^{x}} \right )$, what is the area bounded by $f\left ( x \right )$ for the interval $\left [ 0,2 \right ]$ on the $x$ – axis?

  1. $\frac{1}{2}$
  2. $1$
  3. $2$
  4. $4$

A square with sides of length $6 \mathrm{~cm} $ is given. The boundary of the shaded region is defined by two semi-circles whose diameters are the sides of the square, as shown. 

The area of the shaded region is_______ $\mathrm{cm}^2.$

  1. $6 \pi$
  2. $18$
  3. $20$
  4. $9 \pi$

In a $12$-hour clock that runs correctly, how many times do the second, minute, and hour hands of the clock coincide, in a $12$-hour duration from $3$ PM in a day to $3$ AM the next day?

  1. $11$
  2. $12$
  3. $144$
  4. $2$

Ten teams participate in a tournament. Every team plays each of the other teams twice. The total number of matches to be played is  

  1. $20$
  2. $45$
  3. $60$
  4. $90$

Leila aspires to buy a car worth $Rs. 10,00,000$ after $5$ years. What is the minimum amount in Rupees that she should deposit now in a bank which offers $10\%$ annual rate of interest, if the interest was compounded annually?

  1. $5,00,000 $
  2. $6,21,000$
  3. $6,66,667$
  4. $7,50,000$

In a factory, two machines $M1$ and $M2$ manufacture $60\%$ and $40\%$ of the autocomponents respectively. Out of the total production, $2\%$ of $M1$ and $3\%$ of $M2$ are found to be defective. If a randomly drawn autocomponent from the combined lot is found defective, what is the probability that it was manufactured by $M2$?

  1. $0.35$
  2. $0.45$
  3. $0.5$
  4. $0.4$

A contour line joins locations having the same height above the mean sea level. The following is a contour plot of a geographical region. Contour lines are shown at $25$ m intervals in this plot.

The path from $P$ to $Q$ is best described by

  1. Up-Down-Up-Down
  2. Down-Up-Down-Up

If $\text{P, Q, R, S}$ are four individuals, how many teams of size exceeding one can be formed, with $\text{Q}$ as a member?

  1. $5$
  2. $6$
  3. $7$
  4. $8$

A cab was involved in a hit and run accident at night. You are given the following data about the cabs in the city and the accident.

  1. $85\%$ of cabs in the city are green and the remaining cabs are blue.
  2. A witness identified the cab involved in the accident as blue.
  3. It is known that a witness can correctly identify the cab colour only 80% of the time.

Which of the following options is closest to the probability that the accident was caused by a blue cab?

  1. $12\%$
  2. $15\%$
  3. $41\%$
  4. $80\%$

A $100 \mathrm{~cm} \times 32 \mathrm{~cm}$ rectangular sheet is folded $5$ times. Each time the sheet is folded, the long edge aligns with its opposite side. Eventually, the folded sheet is a rectangle of dimensions $100 \mathrm{~cm} \times 1 \mathrm{~cm}$.

The total number of creases visible when the sheet is unfolded is ___________.

  1. $32$
  2. $5$
  3. $31$
  4. $63$

An opaque cylinder (shown below) is suspended in the path of a parallel beam of light, such that its shadow is cast on a screen oriented perpendicular to the direction of the light beam. The cylinder can be reoriented in any direction within the light beam. Under these conditions, which one of the shadows $\mathbf{P}, \mathbf{Q}, \mathbf{R}$, and $\mathbf{S}$ is NOT possible?

  1. $\mathrm{P}$
  2. $\mathrm{Q}$
  3. $\mathrm{R}$
  4. $\mathrm{S}$

For a regular polygon having $10$ sides, the interior angle between the sides of the polygon, in degrees, is:

  1. $396$
  2. $324$
  3. $216$
  4. $144$

The expression $\dfrac{(x+y) - |x-y|}{2}$ is equal to :

  1. The maximum of $x$ and $y$
  2. The minimum of $x$ and $y$
  3. $1$

Refer to the following pie chart and answer the questions that follow.

  1. $5 \%$ of total cost
  2. $10 \%$ of total cost
  3. $12 \%$ of total cost
  4. $15\%$ of total cost

$\text{A}$ can complete a piece of work in $4$ days. $\text{B}$ takes double the time taken by $\text{A, C}$ takes double that of $\text{B},$ and $\text{D}$ takes double that of $\text{C}$ to complete the same task. They are paired in groups of two each. One pair takes two-thirds the time needed by the second pair to complete the work. Which is the first pair?

  1. $\text{A, B}$
  2. $\text{A, C}$
  3. $\text{B, C}$
  4. $\text{A, D}$

Two alloys $\text{A}$ and $\text{B}$ contain copper and zinc in the ratio $7: 2$ and $5: 3$ respectively. How many kg of $\text{A}$ and $\text{B}$ must be melted in order to get an alloy of $44 \mathrm{~kg}$ containing copper and Zinc in the ratio $3: 1?$

  1. $24 \mathrm{~kg}, 20 \mathrm{~kg}$
  2. $30 \mathrm{~kg}, 14 \mathrm{~kg}$
  3. $28 \mathrm{~kg}, 16 \mathrm{~kg}$
  4. $36 \mathrm{~kg}, 8 \mathrm{~kg}$

​​If ' $\rightarrow$ ' denotes increasing order of intensity, then the meaning of the words [smile $\rightarrow$ giggle $\rightarrow$ laugh] is analogous to [disapprove $\rightarrow$ _________$\rightarrow$ chide]

Which one of the given options is appropriate to fill the blank?

  1. reprove
  2. praise
  3. reprise
  4. grieve

A circular sheet of paper is folded along the lines in the directions shown. The paper, after being punched in the final folded state as shown and unfolded in the reverse order of folding, will look like _______.

Let $x, y$ be two positive numbers such that $x + y =1.$ Then, the minimum value of $\left(x+ \dfrac{1}{x} \right)^2 + \left(y + \dfrac{1}{y}\right)^2$ is

  1. $12$
  2. $20$
  3. $12.5$
  4. $13.3$

There are $150$ students in a class. The number of students who play Cricket, Hockey, and Basketball are $125, 130, 135$ respectively. If $5$ students do not play any of the three games, the number of students playing all the three games must be at least

  1. $90$
  2. $95$
  3. $100$
  4. $105$

In the given text, the blanks are numbered $\text{(i)-(iv)}$. Select the best match for all the blanks.

Prof. $\text{P}$  __(i)__   merely a man who narrated funny stories. __(ii)__ in his blackest moments he was capable of self-deprecating humor.

Prof. $\text{Q}$ ___(iii)__ a man who hardly narrated funny stories. ___(iv)___ in his blackest moments was he able to find humor.

  1. (i) was (ii) Only (iii) wasn't (iv) Even
  2. (i) wasn't (ii) Even (iii) was (iv) Only
  3. (i) was (ii) Even (iii) wasn't (iv) Only
  4. (i) wasn't (ii) Only (iii) was (iv) Even

Connotation of a road or way

  1. Pertinacious
  2. Viaticum
  3. Clandestine
  4. Ravenous

Exhort

Indian currency notes show the denomination indicated in at least seventeen languages. If this is not an indication of the nation's diversity, nothing else is.

Which of the following can be logically inferred from the above sentences?

  1. India is a country of exactly seventeen languages.
  2. Linguistic pluralism is the only indicator of a nation's diversity.
  3. Indian currency notes have sufficient space for all the Indian languages.
  4. Linguistic pluralism is strong evidence of India's diversity.

The policeman asked the victim of a theft, "What did you ___ ?"

  1. Loose
  2. Lose
  3. Loss
  4. Louse

Which of the following statements is/are true?

  1. $(a \rightarrow b)$ always equals $\overline{a}+b$
  2. $(\overline{a}+b)+(a * \overline{b})$ is a tautology
  3. $(a \rightarrow b) *(a * \overline{b})$ is satisfiable

 

  1. III only
  2. I and II only
  3. II and III only
  4. I, II, and III

Consider the premises below which are assumed to be true:
$$
\begin{aligned}
& p \rightarrow(q \wedge r) \\
& \sim p \rightarrow \sim r \\
& \sim p \wedge(r \rightarrow \sim p)
\end{aligned}
$$
Which of the following conclusions would make the argument valid?

  1. $p \rightarrow q$
  2. $\sim p \vee \sim r$
  3. $q \rightarrow(p \rightarrow r)$
  4. $\sim p \wedge \sim q \wedge r$ 
 
  1. Only (i) and (iii).
  2. Only (ii) and (iv).
  3. Only (i), (ii) and (iii).
  4. Only (i), (ii) and (iv).

Consider the statement $\text{S} :$ "For all natural numbers $n,$ if $n$ is prime, then $n$ is antisocial."
You do not need to know what antisocial means for this problem, just that it is a property that some numbers have and others do not.
Assume that we know that natural number $10$ is not a prime number$, \&$ that natural number $7$ is a prime number.

Which of the following statements can be inferred from the statement $\mathrm{S}?$

  1. $10$ is antisocial.
  2. $10$ is not antisocial.
  3. $7$ is antisocial.
  4. $7$ is not antisocial.

Suppose 10 balls are thrown into 10 bins, where each ball is equally likely to land in any one of the 10 bins. The bins are numbered 1 to 10. Let:

  •   $X_{1}$ : Number of balls that land in bin 1.
  •   $X_{2}$ : Number of balls that land in bin 2.
  •   Similarly, $X_{3}, X_{4}, \ldots, X_{10}$.

Define $Z$ as the maximum number of balls in any single bin:
$Z=\max \left(X_{1}, X_{2}, \ldots, X_{10}\right)$.

What is the probability that $Z=1$?

  1. $\frac{9!}{10^{10}}$
     
  2. $\frac{10!}{10^{10}}$
     
  3. $\frac{10}{10^{10}}$
     
  4. $\frac{1}{10}$

James Bond is playing a game that involves repeatedly rolling a fair standard 6-sided die. What is the expected number of rolls until he gets a 5 ?

  1. $1$
  2. $3.5$
  3. $5$
  4. $6$

Let $X$ be a random variable (RV) that takes values $-1$ and $1,$ with $P(X=-1)=\dfrac{1}{2}$. What is the expected value $E\left[X^{2}\right]$?

  1. 1
  2. 0
  3. -1
  4. None of the above.

Let $\mathbf{Z}$ be the group of all integers under the operation of addition. How many of the following subsets of $\mathbf{Z}$ are NOT a subgroup of $\mathbf{Z}?$

  1. $\{0\}$
  2. $\{n \in \mathbf{Z} : n > 0\}$
  3. $\{n \in \mathbf{Z} : n\;\text{is an even integer}\}$
  4. $\{n \in \mathbf{Z} : n \;\text{is divisible by both 6 and 9}\}$

 

  1. $1$
  2. $2$
  3. $3$
  4. $4$

What is the smallest positive integer $n$ such that there is a group of order $n$ which is not abelian?

  1. $4$
  2. $5$
  3. $6$
  4. $7$

Suppose that $S$ and $T$ are sets. Which of the following first-order logic statements are translations of the statement " $S$ is not a subset of $T$ ?" Check all that apply.

  1. $ orall x .(x \in S ightarrow x otin T)$
  2. $ orall x .(x \in S \wedge x otin T)$
  3. $\exists x .(x \in S ightarrow x otin T)$
  4. $\exists x .(x \in S \wedge x otin T)$

Which one of the following is a closed form expression for the generating function of the sequence $\{a_n\}$, where $a_n = 2n +3 \text{ for all } n=0, 1, 2, \dots$?

  1. $\frac{3}{(1-x)^2}$
  2. $\frac{3x}{(1-x)^2}$
  3. $\frac{2-x}{(1-x)^2}$
  4. $\frac{3-x}{(1-x)^2}$

The number of $4$ digit numbers having their digits in non-decreasing order (from left to right) constructed by using the digits belonging to the set $\{1, 2, 3\}$ is ________.

  1. $12$
  2. $15$
  3. $18$
  4. $21$

The triangular graph of order $n\geq 3$, denoted $\text{T}_n$, is a graph defined as follows.

Begin with the set $\{1,2,3, \ldots, n\}$, where $n\geq 3$. The nodes in $\text{T}_n$ are the two-element subsets of $\{1,2,3, \ldots, n\}$, and there's an edge between any two sets that have exactly one element in common.

The number of edges in $\text{T}_n$ for $n=8?$

  1. 1.84
  2. 2.186
  3. 3.336
  4. 4.None of these

How many of the following statements are true?
 

  1.  The graph $K_{2,4}$ is a planar graph.
  2.  The graph $K_{3,4}$ is a planar graph.
  3.  There exists a simple graph that is connected and planar with 5 vertices and 8 faces.
  4. The graph $K_{5}-\{e\}$ where $e$ is any edge in the graph is 4-colourable. 
  1. 1
  2. 2
  3. 3
  4. 4

Perform the following operations on the matrix $\begin{bmatrix} 3 & 4 & 45 \\ 7 & 9 & 105 \\ 13 & 2 & 195 \end{bmatrix}$

  1. Add the third row to the second row
  2. Subtract the third column from the first column.

The determinant of the resultant matrix is _____.

B.1

$$\begin{bmatrix} 1 &2 &3 \\ 1& 3 &4 \\ 2& 2 &3 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} x\\y \\ z \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 6\\8 \\ 12 \end{bmatrix}$$

  2. $x = 12$, $y = 3$, $z = - 4$
  3. $x = 6$, $y = 6$, $z = - 4$

  1. The value of $K$ obtained using the trapezoidal rule is always greater than or equal to the exact value of the definite integral.
  2. The value of $K$ obtained using the Simpson's rule is always equal to the exact value of the definite integral.

Consider a function whose derivative is given by $f^{\prime}(x)=x(x-1)$.
How many of the following option are TRUE about the function?

  1. There is a local max at $x=0$
  2. There is a local min at $x=0$
  3. There is a local $\max$ at $x=1$

  2. $2$
  3. $3$
  4. $4$

$$
\lim _{x \rightarrow 1} \frac{x-1}{\sqrt{2 x+23}-5}
$$

  1. $\dfrac{5}{2}$

\[
\int_{-3}^{3} \int_{-2}^{2} \int_{-1}^{1}\left(4 x^{2} y-z^{3}\right) \mathrm{d} z \mathrm{~d} y \mathrm{~d} x
\]

A $3$ bit down counter is used to control the output of the multiplexer as shown in the figure. The counter is initially at $A_{2} A_{1} A_{0}=101$, the output of multiplexer will follow the sequence:(Output of mux is controlled by select lines, $S1S0)$

Consider a $4$ input boolean function $\mathrm{F}(\mathrm{X}, \mathrm{Y}, \mathrm{Z}, \mathrm{T})$.

The minterm $\mathrm{X}^{\prime} \mathrm{Y}^{\prime} \mathrm{Z}^{\prime} \mathrm{T}^{\prime}$ is known to be in the SOP form of $\mathrm{F}$. Canonical SOP form of function $F$ itself is the minimized SOP form of $F,$ and $F$ is largest such function i.e. Canonical SOP form of $F$ has maximum number of minterms possible. How many of the following are TRUE?

  1. Number of Prime Implicants in $F$ is the same as the number of prime implicants in $F'.$
  2. Minimized SOP, Minimized POS form of $F$ have the same number of literals.
  3. Every implicant of $F$ is a Prime Implicant.
  4. $\mathrm{F}=\mathrm{X} \oplus \mathrm{Y} \oplus \mathrm{Z} \oplus \mathrm{T}$

 

  1. $1$
  2. $2$
  3. $3$
  4. $4$

$F$ is a boolean function in five boolean variables $a,b,c, d$ and $e$.
$$F(a,b,c,d,e)=\sum(0,1,7,8,14,15,16,17,29,30,31)$$
Let $D$ be the Dual of function $F$. Then which of the following is Not a subset of (true) minterms of $D?$

  1. $3,\;4,\;5,\;6,\;27,\;28$
  2. $7,\;8$
  3. $3,\;4,\;5,\;6,\;7,\;8$
  4. $3,\;4,\;7,\;8,\;23,\;24,\;29$

Consider a Boolean function $f(w,x,y,z)$ such that $$\begin{array}{lll} f(w,0,0,z) & = & 1 \\ f(1,x,1,z) & =& x+z \\  f(w,1,y,z) & = & wz +y \end{array}$$The number of literals in the minimal sum-of-products expression of $f$ is _________

  1. $5$
  2. $6$
  3. $7$
  4. $8$

The time taken to access a file that is stored on a hard disk is affected significantly by how data is stored on disks. The bottleneck of a disk access is moving the read/write arm. So it makes sense to store a file in tracks that are below/above each other in different surfaces, rather than in several tracks in the same surface.
Consider a file with $50,000$ records of fixed length, $256$ bytes per record. This file is stored on a hard disk in which we have $512$ bytes per sector, $63$ sectors per track, $16$ tracks per cylinder, and total $4092$ cylinders. File is stored in consecutive cylinders in such a way that first it is stored in a cylinder then in adjacent cylinder and so on. How many cylinder are needed to store this file?

  1. $26$
  2. $20.60$
  3. $24.80$
  4. $30.50$

A $3.5$ inch micro floppy high density disk contains the data _________ .

  1. $720 \: MB$
